## Statement

[View PDF](pdf/main.pdf) · [Download LaTeX source](latex/main.tex)

### Abstract

Fix a random function table $H : \mathcal{K}\times\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{R}$ (a "seeded" random oracle) and a *computationally unbounded* source $S$ that outputs an input $x\in\mathcal{D}$ together with auxiliary information $z$, such that no unbounded predictor can guess $x$ from $(H,z)$ with probability better than $\epsilon$. Two conjectures ask how well $H(\mathit{sd},x)$ for a fresh random seed $\mathit{sd}$ then looks like a uniform output, in two models that differ only in whether the distinguisher is handed the seed: kept secret, or made public. Both conjectured bounds have the shape of the classical leftover hash lemma, splitting the extraction error into an "entropy deficiency" term and a "seed collision" term that vanishes as $1/\sqrt{K}$ in the number of seeds $K$.

### Setting

Fix nonempty finite sets $\mathcal{K}$ (seeds), $\mathcal{D}$ (inputs), $\mathcal{R}$ (outputs), and write $K := |\mathcal{K}|$, $D := |\mathcal{D}|$, $R := |\mathcal{R}|$. Let $\mathsf{Fun}(\mathcal{K}\times\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R})$ be the set of all functions $\mathcal{K}\times\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{R}$, let $\mathrm{SD}(\cdot,\cdot)$ denote statistical distance, and $U_\mathcal{R}$ the uniform distribution on $\mathcal{R}$. The source $S$, the predictor $P$, and the distinguisher $\mathsf{D}$ below are all computationally unbounded and receive the *entire* function table of $H$ as an explicit input. The two extraction games differ only in whether the seed $\mathit{sd}$ is kept secret from $\mathsf{D}$ or given to it.

```{=html}
<table class="cj-game-table">
<tbody>
<tr>
<th>Game \(\mathsf{Pred}^{S}_{P}\)</th>
<th>Game \(\mathsf{Ext}^{S}_{\mathsf{D}}\) (secret seed)</th>
<th>Game \(\mathsf{Ext\text{-}pub}^{S}_{\mathsf{D}}\) (public seed)</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>
\(H \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathsf{Fun}(\mathcal{K}\times\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R})\)<br>
\((x,z) \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} S(H)\)<br>
\(x' \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} P(H,z)\)<br>
<b>return</b> \((x = x')\)
</td>
<td>
\(H \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathsf{Fun}(\mathcal{K}\times\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R})\)<br>
\((x,z) \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} S(H)\); &nbsp; \(\mathit{sd} \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathcal{K}\)<br>
\(y_0 \leftarrow H(\mathit{sd},x)\); &nbsp; \(y_1 \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathcal{R}\)<br>
\(b \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \{0,1\}\)<br>
\(b' \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathsf{D}(H, y_b, z)\)<br>
<b>return</b> \((b = b')\)
</td>
<td>
\(H \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathsf{Fun}(\mathcal{K}\times\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R})\)<br>
\((x,z) \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} S(H)\); &nbsp; \(\mathit{sd} \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathcal{K}\)<br>
\(y_0 \leftarrow H(\mathit{sd},x)\); &nbsp; \(y_1 \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathcal{R}\)<br>
\(b \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \{0,1\}\)<br>
\(b' \stackrel{\$}{\leftarrow} \mathsf{D}(H, \mathit{sd}, y_b, z)\)<br>
<b>return</b> \((b = b')\)
</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
```

Prediction game (left) and the two extraction games: secret seed (middle) and public seed (right). The first argument of $S$, $P$, and $\mathsf{D}$ is the *full function table* of $H$; the games $\mathsf{Ext}$ and $\mathsf{Ext\text{-}pub}$ differ only in whether $\mathsf{D}$ receives $\mathit{sd}$.

::: {.callout-note title="Definition (Advantages and Unpredictability)"}
Set $\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{pred}}_{\mathcal{K},\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R},S}(P) := \Pr[\mathsf{Pred}^{S}_{P} \Rightarrow 1]$ and
$$
\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{\mathcal{K},\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R}}(S,\mathsf{D}) := 2\Pr[\mathsf{Ext}^{S}_{\mathsf{D}} \Rightarrow 1] - 1 ,
\qquad
\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext\text{-}pub}}_{\mathcal{K},\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R}}(S,\mathsf{D}) := 2\Pr[\mathsf{Ext\text{-}pub}^{S}_{\mathsf{D}} \Rightarrow 1] - 1 .
$$
A source $S$ is *$\epsilon$-unpredictable* if $\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{pred}}_{\mathcal{K},\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R},S}(P) \le \epsilon$ for every unbounded predictor $P$.
:::

### The Two Conjectures

::: {.callout-important title="Conjecture 1 (Secret seed)"}
There is a universal constant $c > 0$, independent of $\mathcal{K}$, $\mathcal{D}$, $\mathcal{R}$ and $\epsilon$, such that for all nonempty finite $\mathcal{K}, \mathcal{D}, \mathcal{R}$, all $\epsilon \in (0,1]$, every $\epsilon$-unpredictable source $S$, and every unbounded distinguisher $\mathsf{D}$,
$$
\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext}}_{\mathcal{K},\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R}}(S,\mathsf{D})
\;\le\; \delta(\epsilon, K, D, R)
\;:=\; c \cdot \sqrt{\frac{\epsilon R + \log_2 D}{K}} \; .
$$
:::

::: {.callout-important title="Conjecture 2 (Public seed)"}
There is a universal constant $c > 0$, independent of $\mathcal{K}$, $\mathcal{D}$, $\mathcal{R}$ and $\epsilon$, such that for all nonempty finite $\mathcal{K}, \mathcal{D}, \mathcal{R}$, all $\epsilon \in (0,1]$, every $\epsilon$-unpredictable source $S$, and every unbounded distinguisher $\mathsf{D}$,
$$
\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext\text{-}pub}}_{\mathcal{K},\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R}}(S,\mathsf{D})
\;\le\; \delta_{\mathrm{pub}}(\epsilon, K, D, R)
\;:=\; c \cdot \Bigl( \sqrt{\epsilon R} + \sqrt{\frac{\log_2 D}{K}} \,\Bigr) .
$$
:::

## Proof

[View PDF](pdf/proof.pdf) · [Download LaTeX source](latex/proof.tex)

*AI: Claude Opus 5 (Anthropic) · Prompted by: Pooya Farshim · Reviewed by: nobody yet · 14 August 2026.*

**Scope.** This note resolves **Conjecture 2 (public seed)** — it is proven true, with $c = 2$ (in fact $c=\tfrac85$ suffices, and the smallest constant obtainable by this route is $\approx 1.5615$). It does *not* address **Conjecture 1 (secret seed)**, which remains open here: the note only cites, for comparison, a bound attributed to a separate "companion note" on the hidden-seed game — that companion note is not included on this page and its claim has not been independently checked as part of this resolution. Along the way, the note also shows that the most natural guess for a public-seed bound — literally transposing Conjecture 1's expression from $\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext}}$ to $\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext\text{-}pub}}$ — is **false**, which is what motivates the corrected bound below and is a useful negative result in its own right.

### The conjectured bound is false in this model

::: {.callout-note title="Proposition (Counterexample to the naive transposition)"}
For every $c > 0$ there are nonempty finite $\mathcal{K}, \mathcal{D}, \mathcal{R}$, a value $\epsilon \in (0,1]$, an $\epsilon$-unpredictable source $S$, and a distinguisher $\mathsf{D}$ with
$$
\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext\text{-}pub}}_{\mathcal{K},\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R}}(S,\mathsf{D}) \;\ge\; \tfrac14 \;>\; c\,\sqrt{\frac{\epsilon R + \log_2 D}{K}} \;.
$$
The witness has $z = \bot$ and $X$ uniform on all of $\mathcal{D}$ — the largest entropy a source over $\mathcal{D}$ can have — with $R = D$; $\mathsf{D}$ simply checks whether its challenge lies in the image of the row $H(\mathit{sd},\cdot)$, which it can compute in full since it holds both $H$ and $\mathit{sd}$. Since $\delta(\epsilon,K,D,R)$ can be pushed below $\tfrac14$ by taking $K$ large with everything else fixed, no universal constant $c$ can make the transposed bound hold uniformly in $K$.
:::

Once the seed is public, the map $x \mapsto H(\mathit{sd},x)$ is known to $\mathsf{D}$ in full, so the only randomness left is that of $X$ itself — the seed can no longer contribute entropy, and any correct bound must contain a term in $\epsilon R$ that does not decay in $K$.

### The corrected bound

::: {.callout-important title="Theorem (Corrected public-seed bound)"}
For all nonempty finite $\mathcal{K}, \mathcal{D}, \mathcal{R}$, all $\epsilon \in (0,1]$, every $\epsilon$-unpredictable source $S$, and every unbounded distinguisher $\mathsf{D}$,
$$
\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext\text{-}pub}}_{\mathcal{K},\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R}}(S,\mathsf{D})
\;\le\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{\epsilon R} \;+\; \frac{6}{5}\sqrt{\frac{1 + \ln D}{K}}
\;\le\; 2\sqrt{\epsilon R + \frac{\log_2 D}{K}} \; ,
$$
and also, in a form sharper for large $D$ or $\epsilon$ near its minimum $1/D$,
$$
\mathbf{Adv}^{\mathrm{ext\text{-}pub}}_{\mathcal{K},\mathcal{D},\mathcal{R}}(S,\mathsf{D})
\;\le\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{\epsilon R} \;+\; \sqrt{\frac{\ln(2eD\epsilon)}{2K}} \;+\; \frac{9}{10\sqrt{K}} \; .
$$
:::

Publishing the seed costs exactly one factor of $K$, and costs it in one summand only: the $\sqrt{\epsilon R}$ term (entropy deficiency) does not improve as the seed space grows, while the second term (adversarial selection over which support to attack) keeps its $1/K$ in full. Proving this is a four-step argument — flatten the source to a fixed-size support, compute the mean statistical distance for one fixed support, control the deviation uniformly over *all* supports of all sizes via a bounded-differences (McDiarmid) concentration bound, and average — carried out in full in the linked PDF (Sections 3–4 there).

::: {.callout-note title="Corollary (Conjecture 2 holds)"}
For all nonempty finite $\mathcal{K}, \mathcal{D}, \mathcal{R}$ with $D \ge 2$, all $\epsilon \in (0,1]$, every $\epsilon$-unpredictable source $S$, and every unbounded distinguisher $\mathsf{D}$, Conjecture 2's bound $\delta_{\mathrm{pub}}$ holds with $c = \tfrac85$; the smallest constant obtainable by this route is $\tfrac65\sqrt{1+\ln 2} \approx 1.5615$, attained at $D = 2$. For $D = 1$ it holds with $c = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt2} + \tfrac65 < 1.91$. So $c = 2$ suffices throughout the range in which an $\epsilon$-unpredictable source exists — **Conjecture 2 is proven.**
:::

Conjecture 1's expression is strictly stronger than Conjecture 2's whenever both are compared directly (since $\sqrt{(\epsilon R + \log_2 D)/K} \le \sqrt{\epsilon R} + \sqrt{\log_2 D/K}$), so the Proposition above refutes only the transposition of Conjecture 1 to the public-seed game, not Conjecture 2 itself, which is what the Corollary proves.

## Formal Artifact

Neither conjecture has been formalized in Lean yet.
